Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Implement GitHub issue #199 in indkhan/Moneo: "Read PDFs in chat when Claude is the AI source". Read the issue first (`gh issue view 199`). Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly (tests policy, QA backend only, commit style, never touch the owner's backend/.env or port 3000).

Context: you are in a worktree created from branch `t3/claude-subscription` (PR #201, not yet merged). That PR adds a Claude-plan AI source: `lib/ai/claude.ts` (claudeModel wraps `ai-sdk-provider-claude-code`, which runs the Claude Agent SDK's bundled Claude Code with the owner's claude.ai login), `lib/ai/provider.ts` (`withTools`, model routing for `claude-…` ids). The adapter only forwards image file parts; a PDF part would be dropped silently, so `app/api/chat/route.ts` currently throws "Claude can read photos here but not PDFs yet…" when a Claude model gets a PDF attachment (search for `application/pdf` in that file).

Goal: make PDFs attached in chat readable by Claude, as they are on ChatGPT, and remove that refusal. Pick the simplest robust approach and say why in the PR. Options: (a) extract the PDF text locally (check whether the repo already has a PDF text/parse dependency, e.g. used by imports in lib/import — prefer an existing one) and send it as a text part, ideally inside the Claude path only (e.g. in `claudeModel`'s per-call prompt conversion in lib/ai/claude.ts, converting `file` parts with mediaType application/pdf to text parts), keeping page boundaries; (b) render pages to images. Scanned PDFs with no text layer must not silently produce an empty answer: say clearly that the PDF has no readable text and suggest photos. Keep it local (no new network calls). Respect existing attachment limits (lib/ai/chat-attachments.ts).

Tests: one focused unit test that would fail if a PDF part is dropped or reaches Claude unconverted (mock the adapter like lib/ai/claude.test.ts does). No UI-copy tests.

Verify: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`. Do NOT make real Claude calls in tests. A single optional manual check on the QA backend is fine but not required.

Deliver: commit in small plain-language commits (end each message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`), push a new branch `t3/claude-pdf`, and open a PR with base `t3/claude-subscription` (stacked on PR #201) that says "Closes #199" and ends with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". Never merge. Your final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.
